topic: security/privacy; local differential privacy; dependence detection
status: bounded integration lead; broad novelty claims rejected
claim: Private joint-dependence tests, empirical directed correlation-induced leakage analysis under LDP, and distributional-shift caveats are separate existing components. A bounded open test is whether a private dependence screen can guide attribute-specific LDP budgets while controlling directed inference leakage and utility under held-out and shifted distributions. This is not a claim that private dependence testing or correlation-aware DP is new.
positive_evidence: The 2026 dHSIC paper gives a DP permutation test with level/consistency/minimax results and selected synthetic/causal-data evaluation.
The 2025 CPL paper studies five LDP mechanisms over four datasets and finds symmetric MI/Pearson summaries can miss directed, mechanism-specific attribute-inference leakage.
The CPL paper explicitly notes that distributional misspecification can make estimates suboptimal and leaves the consequences for future work.
counterevidence: Private conditional-independence testing with theoretical guarantees for continuous conditioning variables predates this cell (Kalemaj et al., arXiv v3 2024).
A 2020 survey already organizes correlated-data privacy methods and challenges, so broad claims that correlation in DP was ignored are false.
The CPL paper reports severe leakage was rare in its four studied datasets; it does not support universal high-risk claims.
dHSIC dependence detection under central DP and attribute inference under local DP are distinct threat models; a test statistic is not an attacker leakage metric.

sources.title: Correlated Data in Differential Privacy: Definition and Analysis

falsifiable_test: Across two multi-attribute datasets and synthetic higher-order dependence, compare Pearson/MI budgeting, DP-dHSIC screening, oracle dependency graph, and uniform LDP. Hold out the calibration distribution, inject temporal/domain shift and asymmetric attribute-inference attacks, and report screen type-I/FDR, directed CPL, utility, and formal privacy guarantees. The lead weakens if screening does not improve a pre-registered utility-at-fixed-leakage curve or shift destroys calibration.
limitations: One frozen six-version cell; methods use different privacy models and cannot be pooled. The four-dataset CPL results are setup-specific; targeted literature follow-up, not systematic review.

topic: security/privacy; differential privacy accounting; adaptive composition
status: bounded engineering/validation lead; underlying validity issue established by prior work
claim: The natural path-wise f-DP filter is invalid under fully adaptive composition without structural ordering conditions, and an approximate GDP alternative is justified in asymptotic low/high subsampling regimes but can underestimate privacy loss at intermediate rates. A practical research target is a regime-aware accountant that checks applicability and falls back to a valid conservative bound outside its proved range; the failure/limitation itself is not a novel claim.
positive_evidence: The f-DP study provides a counterexample and necessary/sufficient Blackwell-chain conditions for validity.
The approximate GDP filter's asymptotic guarantees apply near q→0 or q→1; the paper reports underestimation at q=0.1 and an empirical CDF discrepancy near 0.0125 in a displayed simulation.
The paper explicitly calls moderate-rate tight approximate filters future work and compares only against structurally matched single-order RDP.
counterevidence: The exact theoretical characterization identifies when the natural filter is valid, so a substantial part of the safety check is already formalized.
The approximation is provably useful in its stated asymptotic regimes and can outperform its single-order RDP comparator there.
The intermediate-rate error is shown in a specific analyzed mechanism family/simulation; it is not evidence that deployed privacy accountants generally undercount.

sources.title: f-Differential Privacy Filters: Validity and Approximate Solutions
sources.sections: Blackwell-chain validity theorem, adaptive CLT approximation and Monte Carlo results

falsifiable_test: Implement validity conditions and an asymptotic guard, then test adaptive heterogeneous mechanism sequences over ordered/unordered trade-off curves and subsampling rates from sparse to intermediate to near-one. Compare against high-precision privacy-loss distributions and a valid multi-order RDP bound. Require no underestimation outside declared tolerance and measure fallback utility cost. The lead weakens if existing tools already enforce equivalent checks or guards fail to prevent underestimation.
limitations: One theory paper, with its own explicit conditions and simulation examples; not an audit of deployed accountant software or production DP systems.
